body.p: Claims 1-30 have been previously cancelled. Claims 31, 41, and 42 have been

amended. No new matter has been added. Thus, claims 31-51 are pending in the present application. In view of the above amendments and the following remarks, Applicant respectfully submits that all of the presently pending claims are in condition for allowance.
Claims 31-51 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 101 as directed to an abstract idea without significantly more.

It is respectfully submitted that claim 31 satisfies the requirements of patentability and is thus allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101. According to MPEP 2106, two criteria must be satisfied for a claim to be determined as patentable. First, the claimed invention must be directed to one of the four statutory categories - processes, machines, manufactures, and composition matter. Second, the claimed invention must also qualify as patent-eligible subject matter - i.e., the claim must not be directed to a judicial exception (step 2A) unless the claim as a whole includes additional imitations amounting to significantly more than the exception (step 2B). The Examiner acknowledges that the claim satisfies the first criteria, but contends that the claim is directed to a judicial exception, without significantly more. Applicant respectfully disagrees.
Step 2A is a two-prong analysis: 1) whether the claim recites an abstract idea, law of nature, or a natural phenomenon, and 2) whether the claim recites additional elements that

integrate the judicial exception into a practical application. With respect to the first prong of analysis, the Examiner contends that the claim recites an abstract idea and, in particular, mathematical relationships/calculations. As noted in MPEP 2106.04(a)(2), a claim does not recite a mathematical concept if it is only based on or involves a mathematical concept. The MPEP states "a limitation that is merely based on or involves a mathematical concept described in the specification may not be sufficient to fall into this grouping, provided that the mathematical concept itself is not recited in the claim." It is respectfully submitted that claim 31 clearly does not recite a mathematical relation and/or calculation. For example, the pulmonary pulse transit time is recited as being based on the point in time of the heartbeat and the arrival point in time of the arrival blood pressure pulse to the lungs and the hemodynamic parameter is recited as being based on the pulmonary transit time. It is respectfully submitted that the claim itself does not recite any mathematical concept/relation.
Even if the claim could be determined as reciting an abstract idea, it is respectfully

submitted that any purported recitation is integrated into a practical application and is thus not directed to a judicial exception under prong 2 of the analysis. The purported exception is implemented with or used in conjunction with a particular machine or manufacture that is integral to the claim - i.e., a breathing apparatus of a ventilation system. See MPEP 2106.05(b). The Examiner contends that the sensors and/or breathing apparatus of the ventilation system are unaffected by how the determinations of the claim operate. It is

respectfully submitted, however, that as noted in the Specification, the non-invasive determination of the arrival point in time of the blood pressure pulse to the lungs, the pulmonarypulse transit time based on this arrival time, and the determination of a hemodynamic parameterbased thereon, are clear improvements over current ventilation systems. As would beunderstood by those of skill in the art and as noted in the Specification, monitoring ofhemodynamic parameters of a ventilated patient provides an indication of a patient'scardiovascular function, which has generally been difficult to assess in ventilated patientsbecause of their invasive and/or complicated nature. Thus, it is respectfully submitted that thepurported abstract idea of the recited claim is implemented in a particular machine that hasclearly been improved via the claimed matter. Accordingly, it is submitted that claim 31 is notdirected to a judicial exception under Step 2A.
Furthermore, at the very least, under Step 2B, it is respectfully submitted that the claim includes additional elements amounting to significantly more than the purported judicial

exception. The steps of the recited claim are more than mere data gathering of insignificant extra-solution activity according to MPEP 2106.05(g). As noted above, non-invasive determinations of arrival point in time of blood pressure pulses based to the lung based on respiratory pressure/flow, and pulse transit times determined therefrom, as recited in the claim, is a new, inventive concept. The Specification clearly differentiates between pulmonary-flow induced measurements, as recited in the claim, and traditionally obtained systemic measurements. Thus, it is submitted that the claim provides more than mere data collection and includes an inventive concept - significantly more - such that the claims are allowable over 35 U.S.C. 101.

Accordingly, it is respectfully submitted that claim 31 is allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101 and that the rejection of this claim should be withdrawn. Because claims 32-40 depend from and include all of the limitations of claim 31, it is respectfully submitted that these claims are also allowable.
Claims 41 and 42 recite limitations substantially similar to the limitations of claim 31. Thus, for at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 31, it is

respectfully submitted that claims 41 and 42 are allowable over 35 U.S.C. § 101 and that the rejection of these claims should be withdrawn. Because claims 43-51 depend from and includeall of the limitations of claim 42, it is respectfully submitted that these claims are also allowable.
Claims 31-51 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as indefinite for failing to
particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or joint inventor regards as the invention.

With respect to claims 31 and 42, the Examiner contends that the recited "point in time point in time, thb, of a heartbeat of the subject" does not include any measuring/obtaining steps associated therewith such that the relationship thereof with other-time related parameters is unclear. Claim 31 (and similarly claim 42) has been amended to explicitly recite "determining the point in time, thb, of the heartbeat of the subject".
Also, with respect to claim 31, the Examiner contends that the claim recites "obtaining a respiratory pressure and/or a respiratory flow" such that "the measured respiratory pressure
and/or the respiratory flow" lacks sufficient antecedent basis. Claim 31 has been amended to recite "measuring a respiratory pressure and/or a respiratory flow".
In view of the above amendments, it is respectfully submitted that all of the currently pending claims are in condition for allowance.
Claims 31-39 and 41-50 stand rejected under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) as anticipated by U.S. Patent Appln. Pub. No. 2018/0140252 to Luxon et al. (hereinafter "Luxon").
Specifically, Luxon discloses a respiratory monitor configured to sense an airway

pressure/flow to detect cardiogenic oscillations. Luxon. P. 1, para. [0007]. Luxon describes determining parameters such as relative pulmonary blood flow, relative stroke volume, and/or relative pulmonary artery pressure based on an amplitude and/or area under the curves for pressure/flow. Id. at p. 2, para. [0013] and p. 6, para. [0091]. Cardiogenic oscillations may be gated relative to a length/timing of a single heartbeat. Id. at p. 10, para. [0155]. The Examiner contends that this gating is comparable to determining an arrival point in time of the blood pressure pulse to the lungs. It is respectfully submitted, however, that Luxon does not show or suggest that the cardiogenic oscillations are in any way related to an arrival time of a blood pressure pulse to the lungs. The described gating process merely divides the cardiogenic oscillations relative to a length of each heartbeat. Id. Indeed, Luxon explicitly describes determining parameters based on amplitudes and/or area under the curves of the cariogenic
oscillations. The gating merely allows an average of the cardiogenic oscillations to be taken to get more accurate curve data. Id.

The Examiner points to an embodiment of Luxon which describes determining a pulse transit time. Luxon teaches that the pulse transit time is determined based on the ECG signal and either a heartbeat measured by a pulse oximeter or a peak in cardiogenic oscillation curve. Id. at p. 12, para. [0198]. Luxon, however, does not indicate that the peak of the cardiogenic oscillation curve is indicative of the arrival point in time of the blood pressure pulse to the lung or that this pulse transit time is used to determine a hemodynamic parameter according to the recited claim. Indeed, Luxon describes the pulse transit time as providing different information, which is specifically related to a heart valve opening. Id. It is respectfully submitted that Luxon does not use the pulse transit time determined from the ECG signal and the peak in the cardiogenic oscillation curve to determine a hemodynamic parameter according to the recited claim. As discussed above, Luxon describes using the magnitude of the cardiogenic oscillations to determine (relative) PBP and other hemodynamic parameters, such as relative pulmonary blood flow and relative stroke volume. Specifically, Luxon determines the area under the curves for pressure and/or flow data during a heartbeat cycle, and determines changes in PBP of the patient from changes over time of this area. Id. at p. 2, para. [0013]. Thus, it is submitted that Luxon does not show or suggest determining the parameters via a pulmonary pulse transit time which is determined based upon an arrival point in time of a blood pressure pulse to the lungs, as required by the recited claim.
Similarly claim 42 recites a ventilation system for non-invasive determination of a

hemodynamic parameter of a mechanically ventilated subject based on a point in time, thb, of a heartbeat of the subject and an arrival point in time, tarrpulm, at which a blood pressure pulse caused by the heartbeat reaches the lungs of the subject, the ventilation system comprising "a breathing apparatus mechanically ventilating the subject" along with "at least one pressure sensor measuring a respiratory pressure and/or at least one flow sensor measuring a respiratory flow" and "a computer determining the hemodynamic parameter," wherein the computer is configured to "determine the point in time, thb, of a heartbeat of the subject" and

"determine tarr puim from a change in the measured respiratory pressure and/or the respiratory flow resulting from a change in lung volume caused by the arrival of the blood pressure pulse to the lungs of the subject' along with "determine a pulmonary pulse transit time, PTTpum, for the blood pressure pulse based on tnb and tarr pum" and "determine the hemodynamic parameter based on PTTpum."
For at least the same reasons as discussed above with respect to claim 31, it is

respectfully submitted that claim 42 is not anticipated by Luxon and that the rejection of this claim should be withdrawn. Because claims 43-50 depend from and include all of the limitationsof claim 42, it is respectfully submitted that these claims are also allowable.
Claims 31-51 have been provisionally rejected on the ground of nonstatutory double patenting as unpatentable over claims 45-69 of copending U.S. Patent Application Serial No. 17/250,277.

Applicant respectfully disagrees with the rejection. It is respectfully submitted, however, that Applicant is prepared to file a Terminal Disclaimer, if necessary, once the above-referenced rejections have been overcome.
In view of the foregoing, it is respectfully submitted that all of the currently pending
claims are in condition for allowance. All issues raised by the Examiner having been addressed, an early and favorable action on the merits is earnestly solicited.
Respectfully submitted,
